    freq = defaultdict(int)
    left = 0
    max_length = 0
    
    for right in range(n):

        while freq[arr[right]] > 2:
            freq[arr[left]] -= 1

        if all(count == 2 for count in freq.values()):

    max_length = 0
    
    for right in range(n):

            freq[arr[left]] -= 1
            if freq[arr[left]] == 0:
                del freq[arr[left]]

def longest_subarray_with_even_occurrences(arr):
    n = len(arr)
    if n == 0:
        return 0

    # Dictionary to store the first occurrence of each bitmask
    first_occurrence = {}
    # Bitmask to keep track of the parity of occurrences of each element
    bitmask = 0
    # Variable to store the maximum length of the sub-array
    max_length = 0

    for i in range(n):
        # Update the bitmask by toggling the bit corresponding to arr[i]
        bitmask ^= (1 << arr[i])

        # If the bitmask is 0, it means all elements have appeared an even number of times
        if bitmask == 0:
            max_length = i + 1
        else:
            # If this bitmask has been seen before, calculate the length of the sub-array
            if bitmask in first_occurrence:
                max_length = max(max_length, i - first_occurrence[bitmask])
            else:
                # Store the first occurrence of this bitmask
                first_occurrence[bitmask] = i

    return max_length

    from collections import defaultdict
    
    n = len(arr)
    if n == 0:
        return 0

    last_occurrence = {}
    # Dictionary to store the count of each element in the current window
    count = defaultdict(int)
    
    left = 0
    max_length = 0
    
    for right in range(n):
        element = arr[right]
        count[element] += 1
        
        # If the element appears more than twice, shrink the window from the left
        while count[element] > 2:
            left_element = arr[left]
            count[left_element] -= 1
            left += 1
        
        # Update the maximum length of the subarray found so far
        max_length = max(max_length, right - left + 1)
    
    return max_length
